questions.question: How does alcohol affect you?
options: A) It reduces your concentration.
B) It increases your awareness.
C) It improves your co-ordination.
questions.answer: A) It reduces your concentration.

questions.question: Drink driving
options: A) will not affect your reaction time.
B) may affect your reaction time.
C) may cause you to react faster.
questions.answer: B) may affect your reaction time.

questions.question: Which of the following statements on alcohol and driving is true?
options: A) It is safe to drive as long as you think you are not drunk.
B) It is unsafe to drive after consuming alcohol.
C) It is safe to drive one hour after having the last drink.
questions.answer: B) It is unsafe to drive after consuming alcohol.

questions.question: A person will be disqualified from driving if he is caught
options: A) Driving with a blood alcohol concentration over 80 mg of alcohol/100ml of  blood.
B) Failing to obey a 'Stop' traffic sign.
C) Failing to give way to an ambulance with its siren on.
questions.answer: A) Driving with a blood alcohol concentration over 80 mg of alcohol/100ml of  blood.

questions.question: A driver caught with a blood alcohol concentration over 80 mg of alcohol per 100 ml of blood will
options: A)have to pay a fine.
B) be charged in court.
C) be jailed.
questions.answer: B) be charged in court.

questions.question: After consuming alcohol, you should
options: A) not drive.
B) drive slowly.
C)drive at normal speed.
questions.answer: A) not drive.

questions.question: Any person caught driving with blood alcohol content which exceeds the prescribed  limit will
options: A) have to pay a fine.
B) be charged in court.
C) be given a warning.
questions.answer: B) be charged in court.

questions.question: Drink driving may cause
options: A) Reduce the co-ordination of the control of vehicle.
B) Faster reaction.
C) Increase alertness.
questions.answer: A) Reduce the co-ordination of the control of vehicle.

questions.question: Drinking and driving may cause
options: A) Increase confidence.
B) Loss of proper control of the vehicle.
C) Greater awareness of danger.
questions.answer: B) Loss of proper control of the vehicle.

questions.question: Generally, a small amount of alcohol can make you less safe on the road.
options: A) True.
B) False.
C) Not true, if you were an experience driver.
questions.answer: A) True

questions.question: How does the consumption of alcohol affect a person's driving?
options: A) It enables the driver to make better judgements.
B) It enables the driver to have better vision of the road.
C) It reduces the driver's reaction.
questions.answer: C) It reduces the driver's reaction.

questions.question: If you failed to have a proper control of your vehicle, you could be charged for
options: A) Careless driving.
B) Drink driving.
C) Reckless driving.
questions.answer: B) Drink driving.

questions.question: If you consume alcohol, you should
options: A) Have a coffee then drive home.
B) Go home by public transport.
C) Drive home carefully.
questions.answer: B) Go home by public transport.

questions.question: If you had too much alcohol,
options: A) your ability to drive is impaired.
B) Your reactions are better.
C) Your vision is improved.
questions.answer: A) your ability to drive is impaired.

questions.question: If you intend to drive after attending a function, you should
options: A) Avoid mixing your alcoholic drinks .
B) Avoid drinking alcohol.
C) Drink coffee before drinking alcohol.
questions.answer: B) Avoid drinking alcohol.

questions.question: The penalty for a repeat drink driving offender is
options: A) Fine, disqualification and a mandatory jail sentence.
B) Disqualification only.
C) Fine and disqualification only.
questions.answer: A) Fine, disqualification and a mandatory jail sentence.

questions.question: Drink driving can contribute to accidents because
options: A) Driver's judgement is impaired.
B) Drivers take shorter time to react.
C) Driver's vision is improved.
questions.answer: A) Driver's judgement is impaired.

questions.question: What advice should you give to a driver who has a few alcoholic drinks at a party?
options: A) Drive home carefully and slowly.
B) Go home by public transport.
C) Wait a short while and then drive home.
questions.answer: B) Go home by public transport.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences is TRUE?
options: A) Alcohol makes you a better driver.
B) Alcohol has no effect on the way you drive.
C) Alcohol slows down your reaction reactions when driving.
questions.answer: C) Alcohol slows down your reactions when driving.

questions.question: Which of the following statement on alcohol is true?
options: A) You may decline a breath or blood test
B) Alcohol will not be detected by the breath test after peppermints have been eaten.

questions.answer: C) Even a small amount of alcohol tends to increase the chance of an accident.

questions.question: Which of these can affect your reaction time?
options: A) Drugs
B) Contact lenses.
C) Tinted windows.
questions.answer: A) Drugs

questions.question: When the speed increases while driving round a bend,  the push of the centrifugal force will

B) While negotiating a narrow and winding path

B) Slow down and be ready to stop if necessary
C) Stop Immediately
questions.answer: B) Slow down and be ready to stop if necessary

questions.question: A cyclist with a heavy load is wobbling along the road, you should
options: A) drive closer to warn him it is dangerous
B) give him more space when passing
C) not pass him at all
questions.answer: B) give him more space when passing

questions.question: At road junctions which of the following are most vulnerable ?
options: A) Cyclist, pedestrians and motorcyclists
B) Car drivers
C) Lorry drivers
questions.answer: A) Cyclist, pedestrians and motorcyclists

questions.question: If a cyclist is travelling in an unsteady manner ahead, you should
options: A) Refrain from overtaking the cyclist
B) Give yourself more time in overtaking the cyclist
C) Overtake the cyclist quickly and quietly
questions.answer: B) Give yourself more time in overtaking the cyclist

questions.question: On a two-lane carriageway, you should
options: A) keep to the left lane
B) keep to the outer lane
C) not overtake another vehicle
questions.answer: A) keep to the left lane

questions.question: Switching lanes suddenly or abruptly will
options: A) improve the flow of traffic on the road.
B) cause inconvenience and danger to other motorists.
C) cause wear and tear to the vehicle.
questions.answer: B) cause inconvenience and danger to other motorists.

questions.question: To maintain good lane discipline, you should
options: A) form up correctly into the intended lane before reaching the junction
B) drive between lanes so that you can switch lane easily
C) follow closely to the vehicle in front
questions.answer: A) form up correctly into the intended lane before reaching the junction

questions.question: At a roundabout you notice a cyclist is signaling to turn right ahead, you should
options: A) overtake on the right
B) give the cyclist plenty of room
C) give a horn warning
questions.answer: B) give the cyclist plenty of room

questions.question: How should you overtake cyclists?
options: A) Use your horn just once to warn them
B) Drive slowly and leave plenty of room
C) Overtake them as quickly as possible
questions.answer: B) Drive slowly and leave plenty of room

questions.question: Under what circumstances you may not follow the 'keep left rule' ?
options: A) When travelling at the maximum speed limit of the road.
B) When traffic is light.
C) When your path is obstructed.
questions.answer: C) When your path is obstructed.

questions.question: When a cyclist turns his head to the rear, it indicates that
options: A) He may change his direction.
B) He wants to stop.
C) His rear tyre is punctured.
questions.answer: A) He may change his direction.

questions.question: When about to turn left and there is a cyclist on the left, you should
options: A) Horn to warn him.
B) Drive faster to pass the cyclist.
C) Slow down and allow the cyclist to pass first.
questions.answer: C) Slow down and allow the cyclist to pass first.

questions.question: When driving along a two-way street, you should
options: A) always keep near the centre line of the road
B) not cross the centre line at bends
C) not overtake at all times
questions.answer: B) not cross the centre line at bends

questions.question: When turning right at a one-way street, you should position your vehicle
options: A) In the right hand lane.
B)Just left of the centre of the road.
C) In any lane depending on the traffic conditions.
questions.answer: A) In the right hand lane.

questions.question: When you are overtaking a cyclist , you should leave as much space as you would give a car. What is the main reason for this ?
options: A) The cyclist might get off the bike
B) The cyclist might stop suddenly
C) The cyclist might swerve
questions.answer: C) The cyclist might swerve

questions.question: When you see a young cyclist in front, you should
options: A) ride past it quickly
B) slow down and be prepared  to stop
C) maintain normal speed
questions.answer: B) slow down and be prepared  to stop

questions.question: You are driving on a three-lane carriageway at 80 km/h .There is no traffic ahead. Which lane should you use ?
options: A) Any lane.
B) Middle lane.
C) Left lane.
questions.answer: C) Left lane.

questions.question: You are following a cyclist on an uneven road. You should
options: A) overtake immediately
B) allow extra room in case they swerve to avoid pot-holes
C) follow closely so you can be seen in their mirrors
questions.answer: B) allow extra room in case they swerve to avoid pot-holes

questions.question: You are turning left into a side road.  Cyclists are crossing the road near the junction.  You should
options: A) sound your horn
B) wait for them to cross
C)proceed as normal
questions.answer: B) wait for them to cross

questions.question: You intend to turn left and there is a cyclist ahead on the left, you should
options: A) slow down and allow the cyclist to pass the junction
B) drive faster to avoid the cyclist
C)horn to warn him you are turning left
questions.answer: A) slow down and allow the cyclist to pass the junction

questions.question: You should never attempt to overtake a cyclist
options: A) just before you turn left
B) just before you turn right
C) on a one-way street
questions.answer: A) just before you turn left

questions.question: Reaction distance is the distance travelled from the moment, the
options: A)  brake is applied to the time the vehicle comes to a stop.
B)  hazard is seen to the time the vehicle comes to a stop.
C)  hazard is seen to the time the brake is applied.
questions.answer: C)  hazard is seen to the time the brake is applied.

questions.question: 'The distance travelled' from the moment 'the hazard' is seen to the time 'the brake' is applied is known as the
options: A) Stopping distance.
B) Braking distance.
C) Reaction distance.
questions.answer: C) Reaction distance.

questions.question: Generally, overheating of the engine is largely due to
options: A) long distance driving.
B) poor vehicle maintenance.
C) lack of petrol.
questions.answer: B) poor vehicle maintenance.

questions.question: The engine oil level on the dip stick should be
options: A) below the lower marking.
B) above the upper marking.
C) between the lower and upper markings.
questions.answer: C) between the lower and upper markings.

questions.question: Pre-driving checks
options: A) will reduce the chances of  breakdown.
B) should be done only when the vehicle misfires.
C) are not necessary if it is a new vehicle.
questions.answer: A) will reduce the chances of  breakdown.

questions.question: Which of the following maintenance parts could cause an accident if the fluid level is low?
options: A) Battery.
B) Engine.
C) Brake reservoir.
questions.answer: C) Brake reservoir.

questions.question: The 'Two-second Rule' is a sufficient distance between your vehicle and the car in front when road condition is
options: A) Wet.
B) Good.
C) Hazy.
questions.answer: B) Good.

questions.question: You are on a clear and open road in good weather condition, the distance between you and the vehicle in front should be
options: A) one car's length.
B) two car's length.
C) a two second time gap.
questions.answer: C) a two second time gap.

questions.question: To cool an over-heated engine, you should switch off the engine and
options: A) Open the radiator tank cap immediately.
B) Wait for the engine to cool by itself.
C) Pour water on the engine.
questions.answer: B) Wait for the engine to cool by itself.

questions.question: While reversing you should
options: A) look at the rear view and side view mirrors.
B) look through the rear windscreen.
C) both (A) and (B) above.
questions.answer: C) both (A) and (B) above.

questions.question: The Two-second Rule is a simple check to ensure
options: A) A safe distance for you to move off from a junction.
B) A safe distance between your vehicle and the vehicle in front.
C) A safe length of time to signal before your manoeuvre.
questions.answer: B) A safe distance between your vehicle and the vehicle in front.

questions.question: Reversing from a side road into a main road is
options: A) Allowed if there is no vehicle around.
B) Not allowed for it is unsafe and could cause road accident.
C) Allowed during the daytime only.
questions.answer: B) Not allowed for it is unsafe and could cause road accident.

questions.question: You may overtake another vehicle on the left
options: A) If it is a heavy vehicle.
B) If the driver in front signals his intention to turn right.
C) If you are certain that the vehicle would not change direction.
questions.answer: B) If the driver in front signals his intention to turn right.

questions.question: Using intermittent (on/off) braking to stop a car will
options: A) Give repeated signals to vehicles behind.
B) Confuse other drivers.
C) Reduce the braking effect.
questions.answer: A) Give repeated signals to vehicles behind.

questions.question: The rear view mirror inside the cabin should be adjusted so that
options: A) Only the right hand side of the rear windscreen can be seen in the mirror.
B) Only the left hand side of the rear windscreen can be seen in the mirror.
C) A full view of the rear windscreen can be seen in the mirror.
questions.answer: C) A full view of the rear windscreen can be seen in the mirror.

questions.question: The side mirrors should be adjusted so that
options: A) Part of the car body can be seen in the mirror.
B) No part of the car body can be seen in the mirror.
C) The mirror forms an angle of 45 degree with the car body.
questions.answer: A) Part of the car body can be seen in the mirror.

questions.question: Before moving off from a stationary position, you should
options: A) signal  your intention.
B) lookout for other road users especially those in front and behind.
C) both (A) and (B) above.
questions.answer: C) both (A) and (B) above.

questions.question: When approaching a green traffic light signal at a junction, you must
options: A) Speed up to drive through the junction.
B) Slow down and be prepared to stop.
C) Maintain your speed.
questions.answer: B) Slow down and be prepared to stop.

questions.question: When driving behind a bus, you should
options: A) Keep a longer following distance.
B) Keep the normal following distance.
C) Keep more to the right to have a better view.
questions.answer: A) Keep a longer following distance.

questions.question: When you see green traffic light signal from a distance, you should
options: A) Speed up.
B) Slow down.
C) Carry on at the same speed.
questions.answer: B) Slow down.

questions.question: When approaching a traffic light junction with the amber light flashing, you should
options: A)  Slow down and proceed across the junction only when it is safe to do so.
B)  Speed up in order to pass the junction before the light changes.
C)  Stop at the stop-line and wait for the light to change.
questions.answer: A)  Slow down and proceed across the junction only when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When you are driving along a main road, you should
options: A) Stop at every road junction before proceeding.
B) Accelerate through each junction.
C) Check every side road before you drive past them.
questions.answer: C) Check every side road before you drive past them.

questions.question: When should you start to keep left after overtaking?
options: A) As soon as you are ahead of the overtaken vehicle.
B) When you can see the overtaken vehicle in your left wing mirror.
C) When you can see the overtaken vehicle in your rear view mirror inside the cabin.
questions.answer: C) When you can see the overtaken vehicle in your rear view mirror inside the cabin.

questions.question: In slow moving traffic, you should always
options: A) Sound the horn so that vehicles in front will move faster.
B) Stay in your lane.
C) Move quickly to another lane with a shorter queue.
questions.answer: B) Stay in your lane.

questions.question: When you want to reverse your car to your right, you should turn the steering wheel
options: A) To the right.
B) To the left.
C) First to the left then to the right.
questions.answer: A) To the right.

questions.question: The stopping distance on a wet road is _____ longer than on a dry road.
options: A) 4 times
B) 3 times
C) 2 times
questions.answer: C) 2 times

questions.question: When you are following another vehicle on a wet road, you should keep
options: A) 2 seconds behind.
B) More than 2 seconds behind.
C) Less than 2 seconds behind.
questions.answer: B) More than 2 seconds behind.

questions.question: To avoid skidding on a wet road when stopping, you should always
options: A) Apply intermittent  (on/off) braking technique.
B) Depress the clutch pedal followed by the brake pedal.
C) Depress the brake pedal and apply the handbrake together.
questions.answer: A) Apply intermittent  (on/off) braking technique.

questions.question: The safe following distance is
options: A) 1 car-length for every  6 kmh of your speed.
B) 1 car-length for every 16 kmh of your speed.
C) 1 car-length for every 26 kmh of your speed.
questions.answer: B) 1 car-length for every 16 kmh of your speed.

questions.question: The 'Two-Second Rule' of safe following distance applies to all vehicles travelling at
options: A) slow speed only.
B) fast speed  only.
C) any speed.
questions.answer: C) any speed.

questions.question: In a traffic hold-up, you should
options: A) switch off the engine.
B) use the road shoulder.
C) not change lanes.
questions.answer: C) not change lanes.

questions.question: When you are caught in a traffic jam, you should
options: A) keep close to the vehicle in front.
B) move to lane with a shorter queue.
C) stay in your own lane.
questions.answer: C) stay in your own lane.

questions.question: When passing a parked vehicle, you should leave a safe gap of at least
options: A) 0.3 metre between your vehicle and the parked vehicle.
B) 0.5 metre between your vehicle and the parked vehicle.
C) 1.0 metre between your vehicle and the parked vehicle.
questions.answer: C) 1.0 metre between your vehicle and the parked vehicle.

questions.question: You notice a vehicle trying to pull out between a row of stationary vehicles. You should
options: A) drive on regardless of danger ahead.
B) sound the horn and maintain your speed.
C) slow down and be prepared to stop.
questions.answer: C) slow down and be prepared to stop.

questions.question: When you are approaching a stationary vehicle with a driver in it, you should
options: A) drive past him quickly so as not to obstruct him.
B) slow down a little because he may move out suddenly.
C) drive at the same speed because it is his duty to check passing traffic.
questions.answer: B) slow down a little because he may move out suddenly.

questions.question: When pedestrians are facing traffic on a road without pavement, vehicle should keep a  gap of  at least
options: A) 0.5 metre from the pedestrian.
B) 0.75 metre from the pedestrian.
C) 1 metre from the pedestrian.
questions.answer: C) 1 metre from the pedestrian.

questions.question: When pedestrians are facing away from traffic, vehicles should keep a gap of at least
options: A) 0.5 metre from the pedestrians.
B) 1 meter from the pedestrians.
C) 1.5 metres from pedestrians.
questions.answer: C) 1.5 metres from pedestrians.

questions.question: The engine is often cooled by _______________________
options: A) oil only
B) water, air and oil
C) air only
questions.answer: B) water, air and oil

questions.question: When driving a car you are not familiar with, you should first test
options: A) how fast it can go in the 1st gear.
B) how much space it requires to make a turn.
C) how effective its brakes are.
questions.answer: C) how effective its brakes are.

questions.question: An over-heated engine is usually caused by
options: A) travelling at a high speed over a long distance.
B) running the engine too long while stationary.
C) poor maintenance of the vehicle.
questions.answer: C) poor maintenance of the vehicle.

questions.question: When the traffic light turns green at a junction, you should
options: A)  depress the accelerator hard and move off quickly.
B)  check traffic from right and left before moving off.
C)  only move off when other vehicles move.
questions.answer: B) check traffic from right and left before moving off.

questions.question: When another vehicle is following close behind, you should
options: A) move to the left and allow the vehicle behind to overtake.
B) drive faster so as not to obstruct the vehicle behind.
C) ignore the vehicle if you are travelling at the legal maximum speed.
questions.answer: A) move to the left and allow the vehicle behind to overtake.

questions.question: You want to reverse into a side road.  You are not sure that the area behind your vehicle is clear.  What should you do?
options: A) carry on, assuming it is clear
B) look through the rear window only
C) get out and check
questions.answer: C) get out and check

questions.question: A flashing amber traffic light signal means
options: A) signal is about to be cancelled
B) stop unless you are so close to the stop-line that you cannot stop safety
C) traffic lights signals are out of order
questions.answer: C) traffic lights signals are out of order

questions.question: As you steer (reverse) your vehicle into the parking space, the front of the car will
options: A) Swing in
B) Swing out
C) Remain the same
questions.answer: B) Swing out

questions.question: When you are reversing into the parking lot, the front part of your car swings out, you should
options: A) look out for other traffic including cyclists and pedestrians.
B) look behind only.
C) look at the side mirrors.
questions.answer: A) look out for other traffic including cyclists and pedestrians.

questions.question: Before moving off, you should
options: A) Use your mirrors and signal if necessary
B) Use your mirrors, check your blind spot and signal
C) Signal and move
questions.answer: B) Use your mirrors, check your blind spot and signal

questions.question: Before opening your car door, you should look out for
options: A) passsers-by and other motor vehicles.
B) cyclist and motorcyclist.
C) All the above.
questions.answer: C) All the above.

questions.question: Before overtaking another vehicle, you should signal for at least
options: A) Three  seconds
B) Five seconds
C) Seven seconds
questions.answer: A) Three  seconds

questions.question: How often should you test your brakes ?
options: A) Daily
B) Weekly
C) Monthly
questions.answer: A) Daily

questions.question: If a motorcyclist is trying to overtake you, you should
options: A) Drive faster to prevent the rider from overtaking you
B) Slow down and assist the rider to overtaking safely
C) Signal the driver to overtake on the left
questions.answer: B) Slow down and assist the rider to overtaking safely

questions.question: If the car you are overtaking is drifting in its lane, you should
options: A) Use your horn to warn him
B) Signal him with your hand
C) Overtake it quickly
questions.answer: A) Use your horn to warn him

questions.question: If the foot-brake pedal moves all the way to the floor, it is a sign that the foot-brake
options: A) is working
B) may be faulty
C) is normal
questions.answer: B) may be faulty

questions.question: If the frictional force is reduced on wet road, the stopping distance will be
options: A) The same
B) Longer
C) Shorter
questions.answer: B) Longer

questions.question: If the medicines prescribe by the doctor are likely to affect your driving, you should
options: A) Drive only if someone is with you.
B) Not drive yourself.
C) Avoid driving on the expressway..
questions.answer: B) Not drive yourself.

questions.question: If you are feeling very tired and sleepy whilst driving on an expressway, you should
options: A) Make an exit and stop at a safe place to rest
B) Stop at the road shoulder to rest
C) Switch on hazard lights and drive slowly along the road shoulder
questions.answer: A) Make an exit and stop at a safe place to rest

questions.question: In order to avoid an accident with the vehicle in front while driving under normal conditions you should use the
options: A) Two-second rule
B) Four-second rule
C) Two metre rule
questions.answer: A) Two-second rule

questions.question: The brake system within a vehicle
options: A) Requires little or no maintenance.
B) May be ignored as long as the vehicle stops safely.
C) Neither of these.
questions.answer: C) Neither of these.

questions.question: The light turns red as you approach a traffic junction, when stopping you should
options: A) Depress the brake and the clutch pedals simultaneously
B) Shift to neutral and step on the brakes
C) Brake firmly and depress the clutch pedal as the car comes to a stop
questions.answer: C) Brake firmly and depress the clutch pedal as the car comes to a stop

questions.question: The safe following distance between the front vehicle and your vehicle is
options: A) one car length for every  6  km/h
B) one car length for every 16 km/h
C) one car length for every 26 km/h
questions.answer: B) one car length for every 16 km/h

questions.question: The term 'Tailgating' means
options: A) reversing into a vertical parking lot
B) the dangerous practice of following another vehicle too closely
C) parking at the tail end of the gate or entrance
questions.answer: B) the dangerous practice of following another vehicle too closely

questions.question: The 'two-second rule' is used in normal driving situation at
options: A) Certain speed only
B) All speed
C) Fixed speed only
questions.answer: B) All speed

questions.question: There is a slow moving motorcyclist ahead of you. You are not sure what the rider is going to do, you should
options: A) Pass on the left
B) Pass on the right
C) Stay behind
questions.answer: C) Stay behind

questions.question: To apply intermittent braking, you should depress the brake pedal
options: A) All the way down
B) 2 or 3 times at short intervals before stopping the vehicle
C) And clutch together
questions.answer: B) 2 or 3 times at short intervals before stopping the vehicle

questions.question: To move off safely from a parked position, you should
options: A) signal your intention and move off.
B) look right, left and right again.
C) check mirrors, give signal, look around to check  traffic or pedestrians.
questions.answer: C) check mirrors, give signal, look around to check  traffic or pedestrians.

questions.question: A turn signal that keeps flashing after a turn is very likely to
options: A) confuse other drivers and cause them to turn into your path
B) damage the electrical system
C) keep other drivers from seeing your brake light
questions.answer: A) confuse other drivers and cause them to turn into your path

questions.question: A vehicle loaded with goods
options: A) Requires a longer braking distance than if it were without goods.
B) Does not require a longer braking distance.
C) Brakes normally.
questions.answer: A) Requires a longer braking distance than if it were without goods.

questions.question: As you appoach a controlled junction the lights change to green.  Elderly people are halfway across, you should
options: A) Rev your engine to make them hurry
B) Wait because they will take longer to cross
C) Flash your lights to hurry them
questions.answer: B) Wait because they will take longer to cross

questions.question: Before making a lane change to your left, you must signal for at least 3 second and
options: A) Use your vehicle brake lights to warn other road users
B) Use your vehicle hazard lights to warn other road users
C) Check your blind spot before moving left
questions.answer: C) Check your blind spot before moving left

questions.question: Before reversing, you should check
options: A) Behind
B) All round
C) Ahead and behind
questions.answer: B) All round

questions.question: Before turning right into a minor road, you should
options: A) Slow down or stop to give way to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians
B) Slow down and turn sharply
C) Not give way to oncoming vehicle
questions.answer: A) Slow down or stop to give way to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians

questions.question: Before turning, you need to signal and
options: A) Check your side mirrors only
B) Check your mirrors, as well as blind spots
C) Use your brake lights to warn other road users
questions.answer: B) Check your mirrors, as well as blind spots

questions.question: Before you reverse, you must make sure that there are no
options: A) Other vehicles behind you
B) Children, pedestrian and obstruction in the blind area
C) Both answers above
questions.answer: C) Both answers above

questions.question: Head-on collisions can actually happen at
options: A) any place
B) straight road only
C) junctions and on bends only
questions.answer: A) any place

questions.question: How should you signal  to let others know of your intention?
options: A) At least 2 seconds in advance
B) At least 3 seconds in advance
C) At least 5 seconds in advance
questions.answer: B) At least 3 seconds in advance

questions.question: How should you signal when you want to stop just after a side road to the left?
options: A) give a slowing down arm signal before the junction
B) wait until you have passed the junction, then signal left
C) signal left before the junction
questions.answer: B) wait until you have passed the junction, then signal left

questions.question: How does a school warden signals you to stop?
options: A) by displaying a stop sign
B) by giving you a hand signal
C) by pointing to children on the opposition pavement
questions.answer: A) by displaying a stop sign

questions.question: If you have to downshift for a turn,  you should do it
options: A) Before you start the turn.
B) Just as you begin the turn.
C) While you are in the turn.
questions.answer: A) Before you start the turn.

questions.question: If you saw a sign indicating road repairs are going on, you should
options: A) stop immediately and wait for instructions.
B) slow down and watch out for traffic controllers and instructions.
C) maintain the same speed.
questions.answer: B) slow down and watch out for traffic controllers and instructions.

questions.question: If you turn too late when steering around a corner, you risk
options: A) Swinging wide on left turns
B) Striking the left kerb when turning left
C) Cutting the corner when turning right
questions.answer: A) Swinging wide on left turns

questions.question: If your view is blocked while reversing, you should
options: A) Sound the horn as you reverse
B) Stop and wait until the obstruction is cleared
C) Seek help
questions.answer: C) Seek help

questions.question: To drive in a way where other drivers will not find it necessary to overtake you, you should
options: A) Drive on the extreme right lane all the time
B) Always drive at a speed that match the traffic flow
C) Drive at the maximun speed limit of the road all the time
questions.answer: B) Always drive at a speed that match the traffic flow

questions.question: On rainy day, you should
options: A) Drive at a normal speed
B) Drive as close as possible to the vehicle in front
C) Reduce your speed and keep a longer following distance from the front vehicle
questions.answer: C) Reduce your speed and keep a longer following distance from the front vehicle

questions.question: One of the reasons for you to have an accident with the vehicle you are following is that you
options: A) follow too closely to the vehicle in front
B) follow the vehicle in front with too wide a gap
C) suddenly slow down and stop
questions.answer: A) follow too closely to the vehicle in front

questions.question: The first thing a driver of a motorcar should do before reversing is to
options: A) Release the brakes
B) Take a good look at the traffic behind
C) Release the seat belt
questions.answer: B) Take a good look at the traffic behind

questions.question: The most likely reason for the vehicle  from behind to hit you is that
options: A) it has bald tyres.
B) it follows too closely behind you
C) the driver is still under probation.
questions.answer: B) it follows too closely behind you

questions.question: The stopping distance of a vehicle comprises the
options: A) Thinking distance and the reaction distance
B) Reaction distance and the braking distance
C) Skidding distance and the braking distance
questions.answer: B) Reaction distance and the braking distance

questions.question: To brake safely on a wet road, you should
options: A) apply both brakes together
B) apply intermittent (on/off) braking technique
C) depress the clutch pedal first followed by the brake pedal
questions.answer: B) apply intermittent (on/off) braking technique

questions.question: Using intermittent  braking while stopping your vehicle will
options: A) Save fuel
B) Give sufficient warning to motorists behind of your stopping
C) Prevent tyre wear
questions.answer: B) Give sufficient warning to motorists behind of your stopping

questions.question: What action would you take when elderly people are crossing the road ?
options: A) Wave them across so they know that you have seen them
B) Be patient and allow them to cross in their own time
C) Tap the horn in case they are hard of hearing
questions.answer: B) Be patient and allow them to cross in their own time

questions.question: What is the best choice you have to do at the first sign of drowsiness?
options: A) Slow down and continue at a constant speed
B) Let fresh air gets into the car and at the first opportunity, stop and rest
C) Continue to drive and try to keep awake
questions.answer: B) Let fresh air gets into the car and at the first opportunity, stop and rest

questions.question: What should you do if your brakes were slack or spongy ?
options: A) Ignore them as long as it is effective.
B) Get them checked as soon as possible.
C) Pumps the brake before stopping.
questions.answer: B) Get them checked as soon as possible.

questions.question: When approaching a junction and the traffic lights signal change from green to amber, you should
options: A) stop at the stop line unless you are so close that sudden or sharp braking might cause an accident.
B) speed up to clear the intersection.
C) stop only if a red light camera is in use.
questions.answer: A) stop at the stop line unless you are so close that sudden or sharp braking might cause an accident.
